questions.prompt: A fair six-sided die with faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 is thrown once.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability of obtaining an even number or a number greater than 4.

questions.prompt:
The table below records the primary mode of travel for 80 college students in Years 12 and 13:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Year 12} & \text{Year 13} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Bus} & 18 & 22 & 40 \\ \hline \text{Walk} & 12 & 28 & 40 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 30 & 50 & 80 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A student is selected at random from the 80 students. Find the probability that the student is in Year 13 and walks to college.

questions.prompt: A fair coin and a fair four-sided spinner with faces marked 1, 2, 3, 4 are flipped and spun simultaneously.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: List the sample space of outcomes, and find the probability of obtaining a Head and an odd number.

questions.prompt: In a group of 50 students, 35 study French and 20 study German. Exactly 12 students study both French and German.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the number of students who study neither French nor German, and find the probability that a randomly chosen student studies neither language.

questions.prompt: A biased spinner has three sections labelled 1, 2, and 3. The probabilities of landing on each section are $P(1) = 0.4$, $P(2) = 0.35$, and $P(3) = 0.25$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability of not spinning a 1, and find the probability of spinning a number greater than 1.

questions.prompt: A shop sells 150 laptops: 90 are Brand X and 60 are Brand Y. Of the Brand X laptops, 18 have touchscreen displays. Of the Brand Y laptops, 24 have touchscreen displays.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen laptop has a touchscreen display.

questions.prompt:
The table below shows information about 120 members of a sports club:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Tennis} & \text{Hockey} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Junior} & 26 & 34 & 60 \\ \hline \text{Senior} & 18 & 42 & 60 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 44 & 76 & 120 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A member is chosen at random. Find the probability that the member plays hockey.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the chosen member is a Junior or plays tennis (or both).

questions.prompt:
The table below classifies 200 bicycles in a shop by type and colour:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Red} & \text{Blue} & \text{Green} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Road} & 36 & 44 & 20 & 100 \\ \hline \text{Hybrid} & 24 & 46 & 30 & 100 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 60 & 90 & 50 & 200 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: One bicycle is chosen at random. Find the probability that it is blue or green.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given that the chosen bicycle is a Road bicycle, find the probability that it is red.

questions.prompt: A biased spinner has sections labelled 1, 2, and 3 with probabilities $P(1) = 0.5$, $P(2) = 0.3$, and $P(3) = 0.2$. The spinner is spun and a fair coin is flipped simultaneously. A Head counts as 1 point and a Tail counts as 0 points. The total score $S$ is the spinner value plus the coin value.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: List all pairs of outcomes that result in a total score $S \le 2$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that the total score $S$ is at most 2.

questions.prompt: A fair red die and a fair blue die are rolled simultaneously. Event $A$ is 'the score on the red die is even'. Event $B$ is 'the sum of the scores on the two dice is at least 10'.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: List all outcomes in the event $A \cap B$ as ordered pairs $(\text{red}, \text{blue})$, and find $P(A \cap B)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine whether the events $A$ and $B$ are independent, showing clear mathematical working.

questions.prompt: Of 100 students surveyed about their language options, 65 study Spanish, 45 study Mandarin, and 20 study both languages.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Construct a two-way table displaying the numbers of students studying and not studying Spanish and Mandarin.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A student is selected at random from the 100 students. Find the probability that the student studies exactly one of the two languages, and determine whether studying Spanish and studying Mandarin are independent.

questions.prompt:
Each of the 180 students at a music academy plays exactly one primary instrument: piano, guitar, or drums. The distribution by gender and instrument is given in the table below:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Piano} & \text{Guitar} & \text{Drums} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Male} & 24 & 44 & 12 & 80 \\ \hline \text{Female} & 44 & 38 & 18 & 100 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 68 & 82 & 30 & 180 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A student is chosen at random. Find the probability that the student plays the guitar.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the student is male given that the student plays the drums.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine whether the events 'the student plays the guitar' and 'the student is female' are independent, justifying your answer.

questions.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice, Die A and Die B, each with faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, are rolled simultaneously. Let $X$ be the score on Die A and $Y$ be the score on Die B. Let $E$ be the event that $X + Y = 7$, and let $F$ be the event that $|X - Y| = 1$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: List all outcomes in event $E$ and all outcomes in event $F$ as ordered pairs $(X, Y)$, and find $P(E)$ and $P(F)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find $P(E \cap F)$ and $P(E \cup F)$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine whether the events $E$ and $F$ are independent, giving clear mathematical justification.
